title: GTA 6 Review Roundup: Critics Call It Rockstar's Best
description: GTA 6 review roundup: critics at IGN, GameSpot, The Guardian and more praise Rockstar's huge Leonida open world and its Jason and Lucia love story.

body.text: The first GTA 6 review scores are in, and critics are overwhelmingly positive about Rockstar's long-awaited sequel. According to PC Gamer's roundup, outlets from IGN to The Guardian describe it as the studio's best work, praising its enormous open world and its love story. For Indian players waiting on any word about the game, it is the strongest signal yet of what Rockstar has delivered.
GTA 6 review scores: what critics are saying

PC Gamer says the reviews are glowing across the board. IGN's Luke Reilly gave it a perfect score, which PC Gamer describes as the outlet's second. The only non-perfect score in PC Gamer's sample is Slant's 4.5/5, and that review is still full of praise.

Giant Bomb's Dan Ryckert calls it "Rockstar's best game" and says the studio overdelivered on the most hyped game of all time, after thirteen years between entries. The New York Times doesn't give scores, but it did name the game an NYT Critic's Pick.
Leonida and a world packed with detail

Several reviewers focus on the setting. GameSpot's Tamoor Hussain describes a world of staggering scope that is obsessed with small details. The Guardian's Keza MacDonald says reviewing it feels like trying to review Paris, because it holds so many possible experiences.

Reilly says he finished the game in 120 hours and still hasn't visited large parts of the map. Bloomberg's Jason Schreier compares the joy of discovery to Breath of the Wild and Elden Ring, and describes random events that pull you into elaborate, heightened-reality situations. GamesRadar's Josh West says no part of the series' gameplay hasn't been improved on.

The surprise is how much the reviews talk about the characters. The NYT's Yussef Cole calls it a game about love and relationships, their joy and heartache, and the work needed to make them last. He notes that players can hold hands with their partner at the touch of a button.

Slant's Justin Clark goes further, calling the bond between Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos the first truly meaningful interactive relationship between two semi-realistic adults in the medium. The Guardian says the game mixes foulmouthed, over-the-top chaos with new empathy for the fugitive couple.

These reviews cover the console release. PC Gamer says a PC port is "all-but-certain" but hasn't confirmed one, and its own full review is waiting on that version. So PC players have no confirmed platform or date to plan around yet.

Watch for official word from Rockstar on a PC release, and for further scores from outlets not in this sample. Players will also start finding the small details reviewers keep mentioning, so expect plenty of discoveries to surface once the game is in more hands. Right now, the early verdict is that the hype may have been justified.

faqs.q: What are the GTA 6 review scores?
faqs.a: According to PC Gamer's roundup, IGN gave a perfect score, and the only non-perfect score in its sample was Slant's 4.5/5. The New York Times doesn't score games but named it an NYT Critic's Pick.

faqs.q: Is there a GTA 6 PC version?
faqs.a: PC Gamer calls a PC port "all-but-certain" but doesn't confirm one. It says its own full review will wait for that version, and it has only published impressions of the console release so far.

faqs.q: Who are the main characters in GTA 6?
faqs.a: The protagonists are Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, and the story is set in Leonida. Reviewers, including the NYT's Yussef Cole, single out their relationship as the game's heart.
